1.why: Recovery tokens are bound to the session's recovery record and accountId; verify/reset only accept the tokenHash stored for that recovery.

2.why: The reset token is stored only on the initiating session's recovery object, so the same code does not work for another user/session.

3.why: Password reset updates the account hash and consumes the recovery token but never invalidates or clears other existing sessions.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key, HTTPS is enforced in fetch, and HSTS is set, though TLS version is not explicitly pinned to a named latest release.

5.why: Passwords use bcrypt and reset tokens are stored as SHA-256 digests; protection is appropriate hashing rather than encryption of all user data.

6.why: There is no real email body; the mock delivery path returns and logs the plaintext mockToken, so private reset material is not well guarded in the simulated message.

7.why: Inputs are type/format-validated (validReference, validToken, passwordError) and the UI sets text via textContent rather than injecting raw HTML.

8.why: Navigation is hash/API route based with a fixed allowlist; no user-controlled external redirect targets are honored.

9.why: No email templates render user-supplied HTML/scripts; mock delivery only logs a server-generated token string.

10.why: Recovery/MFA mock tokens are intentionally written to the on-page logs panel and console, so tokens are shown in logs.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed, but the MFA secret is a fixed plaintext code '246810' embedded in source.

12.why: The startup credential is a randomToken(32) value hashed at boot; no fixed default password is accepted.

13.why: Login, recovery verify, and MFA each increment attempts and lock for LOCK_TTL after MAX_ATTEMPTS (5).

14.why: Recovery and login always return the same generic messages whether or not the identifier matches the mock account.

15.why: Reset tokens are randomBytes-based base64url values (24 bytes), hashed at rest, and tied to the specific session recovery/account.
